In summary, our research is concerned with
the ultrastructure of the fibrin-binding site of M protein, which is a major virulence factor of the group A streptoci.
the localization of the fibril binding site in the M protein.
the interaction of the fibrillar M protein on the surface of the streptococcos with fibrinogen.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
M proteins of streptococcus pyogenes are able to bind fibrinogen to its distal end.
the fibrin-binding region of the M protein is located in the distal part of the molecule, and that this region remains exposed after fibrin binding.
the fibrin binding region lies within a 25 nm segment of the fibrilae beginning approximately 35 nm from the inner cell surface, and is located on the amino terminal half of the M molecule.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the fibrin(ogen)-binding region of streptococcus M protein lies within the distal half of the molecule, that it is exposed on the surface of fibrillar M protein molecules, and that it is not blocked by other plasma proteins.

the fibrin binding site is located on the distal end of the M protein, and that the fibrin binds to the M protein in the fibrilae of the cell wall, which is the location where the M protein interacts with complement and the immune system.

the M protein molecule has two distinct regions, the distal region, which binds to fibrinogen and is exposed on the surface of the fibrillar tip, and the proximal region, which binds antibody and is buried within the fibrillar core.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the fibrin-binding region of the M protein is located within a 25- to 50-nm segment of fibrillar tips, and that it is not the same segment as the region of the M molecule that binds opsonic antibody.
the fibrin(ogen)-binding domain is located within 25 nm of the outer cell wall surface.
the fibrin(ogen) binding domain of the M protein is located on the distal portion of the M protein fibrils and is exposed to the environment.
